title: Operator perimeter gate, key-locality verifier and audit rate-cap middleware
author: Marta Alvarez
description:
Context: A recent internal review and a customer audit (Linear: ENG-1124) flagged two gaps: (1) operators with broad service-level RBAC were able to access KMS-backed operations across geozones without an explicit locality assertion, and (2) high-volume audit streams from background operator workflows were spiking ingestion costs and obscuring tenant-facing events. Motivation: introduce a lightweight runtime guard that enforces operator perimeter checks (operator-scoped claims must match service boundary), a KMS key-locality verifier that rejects cross-geozone key use unless explicitly consented, and an audit rate-cap middleware that reduces noisy operator telemetry while preserving forensics for tenant-impacting calls. This PR implements the enforcement shim, KMS-locality proof validator, a tokenized consent header path, and a configurable audit-rate limiter with sampling rules.

What changed (high level): added a runtime perimeter guard integrated into the authz pipeline; implemented a KMS key-locality verifier that consults key metadata and tenant consent caches; added an audit rate-cap middleware that classifies events by risk and routes high-volume operator noise to low-cost archival while preserving spike samples; expanded config to allow per-service policy thresholds and opt-in overrides; E2E test harness + integration tests for locality rejection and audit sampling; docs and migration notes for operators and on-prem installers.

Review thread (abridged):
- Ethan: "Perimeter gate looks good. Two asks: make the locality verifier non-blocking under install-time feature flag and ensure the cache TTL is configurable per-region." (author reply: addressed; added feature_flag.locality_mode and config.kms.cache_ttl_ms). 
- Priya: "Audit sampling strategy: need deterministic sampling windows for forensic replay, and a clear path to increase retention for tenant-impacting calls." (author reply: added spike-sample deterministic sampler and a retention override header; expanded SRE runbook). 
- Noah: "Load profile impact? We need microbench results and CI perf gate." (author reply: included microbench results and added a perf check to PR CI; bench shows 3.1% P50 token latency increase under worst-case with locality checks enabled; default rollout under shadow minimizes impact).
- Security review (internal): "Ensure operator-scoped claims can't be forged by operator-submitted service headers." (author: added signature-validated operator-attestation header and hardened parsing logic).

CI and gating: Full CI (unit/integration/e2e) passed. Additional checks: static analysis (go vet, govet-rules), policy-linter, and a lightweight perf smoke test were added to the pipeline and are green. One flaky test (integration-tests/kms_emulator) flaked on first run; rerun fixed it. All green at merge.

Rollout plan: feature_flag.operator_perimeter defaults to shadow for 48h across staging; after monitoring (alerts for false-positive rate >0.1% or latency P50 drift >5%) the flag will be promoted to enforce in canary region then globally. KMS locality enforcement starts in "audit-only" mode and will require SOC approval to switch to hard-reject. Runbook includes steps to add exceptions via configs/rbac/policies/operator-exceptions.yaml.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: The shim is opt-in by config and can be enabled per-cluster. Existing operator tokens without locality claims will be accepted while locality_mode is "audit-only". Customers using on-prem installer need to upgrade installer package (see docs) to opt into locality attestations.

Merge outcome: squash merge after approvals, linked Linear tickets updated, release notes drafted below.
